title: Regression Sentinel: Automated quality audits for config/model deltas
creator: Asha Mehta
description: After the March 5th production incident where a subtle sampler config change reduced answer coverage for long-context prompts, existing evals missed the regression because the test matrix did not include the affected prefix distributions. This ticket creates a persistent 'Regression Sentinel' that ties config and model deltas to targeted eval runs and alerts. Goals: (1) automatically detect when a config or model change touches a previously uncovered input distribution, (2) trigger focused evals that exercise the impacted slices (prefix lengths, token distributions, response style), and (3) block or flag rollouts until guardrail thresholds are satisfied. The approach favors surgical targeted tests over full-sweep backfills to keep compute costs predictable.
acceptance_criteria: A delta-detector runs on every config/model change and emits a ranked list of impacted eval slices
A CI job consumes the detector output and runs the adaptive re-eval runner against golden snapshots for affected slices
Automated gating: rollouts are blocked if any slice crosses pre-defined regression thresholds (precision/coverage/acceptance)
Dashboards show per-change fingerprints, baseline vs new metrics, and a link to the failing prompt examples
steps: Instrument config change pipeline to record change fingerprints (hash of changed fields + model artifact ID)
Implement coverage-delta detector that compares change fingerprint against historical eval coverage map
Build adaptive re-eval runner that accepts a list of slices and runs targeted evals using golden snapshots
Add CI gating integration: PR -> staging rollout -> detector -> re-eval -> pass/fail decision
Wire alerts to #infra-evals Slack channel with ticketable links and quick triage playbook
Create runbook describing threshold choices, rollback criteria, and compute budget limits
comments: 2025-03-10 Asha Mehta: Created ticket after postmortem call. Root cause: CVT sampler config introduced slight token truncation that reduced coverage on long-prefix templates. Existing smoke evals didn't cover that distribution.

2025-03-11 Carlos Nguyen: Spike implemented for fingerprinting in config-service. Prototype hashes changed fields and model id. Stored example: /tmp/delta-20250311.json. Next: mapping from fingerprint -> coverage buckets.
2025-03-12 Sophie Leroux (PM): Reviewed approach. Asked for explicit compute budget guard and opt-out for low-risk cosmetic changes. Added as acceptance criteria.

2025-03-13 Carlos Nguyen: Pushed branch feat/delta-detector (GH #4021). Early runs show detector correctly classifying 88% of past incident deltas as 'coverage-impacting'. Need to refine slice ranking heuristic.
2025-03-14 Infra review (ops): Verified Slack alert format and escalation path. Suggested adding a TTL to golden snapshots to limit storage costs.
2025-03-15 Asha Mehta: Decided to prioritize targeted eval runner and CI gating for config changes first; full backfill automation deferred to follow-up ticket ENG-21458.
notes: Trade-offs considered: (a) full sweep evals for every change would catch everything but cost too much; (b) only running smoke tests is cheap but misses distributional regressions. Chosen middle path: delta-driven targeted evals + gating. We will iterate on slice definitions (prefix length bins, semantic intent buckets) after first 2 months of runs.
